articleTitle: Load Balancing Optimization in Software-Defined Wide Area Networking (SD-WAN) using Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Software-Defined Wide Area Network (SD-WAN) holds tremendous potential to provide multi-cloud multi-network interconnection and prevent channel congestion. However, traffic among Customer Premises Edge (CPE) and controllers continuously increases, requiring pre-emptive load balancing in the control plane. In this paper, we study the flow migration problem in SD-WANs when the controller presents a limited processing capacity. Specifically, the data plane may include one or more CPE deployed at a site where service traffic is forwarded. To address this narrow, we propose a new approach based on a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) strategy to optimize the balancing process under a latency constraint. As far as we can tell, we have not observed any pertinent research published in this context. The obtained simulation results revealed that our proposed approach decreases the load balancing and outperforms other baseline methods.

articleTitle: Analysis of Vegetation and Penetration Losses in 5G mmWave Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The 5G network has been intensively studied within the early deployment stages as an effort to match the exponential growth of the number of connected devices and users, alongside with their increasing demands for higher throughput, bandwidth, and lower latency. Knowing that most of the frequency spectrum below 6 GHz is saturated, it is not feasible to rely only on the traditional frequency bands that are currently in use. Therefore, a promising solution to combat the insufficient frequency spectrum is to adopt new frequency bands for next-generation mobile communication systems. The primary effort has been focused on utilizing the millimeter-wave (mmWave) bands as the most promising candidate for the frequency spectrum. However, even though the mmWave frequency bands could fulfill the desired bandwidth requirements of 5G, it has been demonstrated to endure several issues such as scattering, atmospheric absorption, fading, and especially penetration losses compared to the existing sub-6 GHz frequency bands. Then, it is fundamental to optimize the mmWave band propagation channel to facilitate the practical 5G implementation for the network operators. In this paper, we simulated different scenarios in order to study the vegetation and penetration loss in 5G systems. Vegetation loss will be studied using the 28 GHz bandwidth and for the penetration loss we will study soft materials <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< 15\mathbf{dB}$</tex> and hard materials <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$> 20\mathbf{dB}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Low Complexity Acoustic Feedback Cancellation Algorithm with Frequency Shifting and Dichotomous Coordinate Descent Iterations
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Numerous acoustic feedback cancellation (AFC) algorithms are used in open-fitting and in-ear hearing aid devices to avoid the possible annoying howling sounds. In this paper, a new algorithm using dichotomous coordinate descent iterations and frequency shifting is proposed. It is shown that the proposed approach has the lowest numerical complexity among the considered competing algorithms and achieves good performances in improving the quality of speech and music signals.

articleTitle: A Home Energy Management System
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Global warming and climate changes have become the world's serious issues, so researchers have focused on analyzing and reducing the energy consumption. Transitioning to renewable energy is one way to help slow down the effects of climate change. In this paper, an energy management system, particularly an energy monitoring system, in a residential house is presented. The system is part of a smart home automation system called qToggle. Energy monitoring systems are considered as next-generation energy saving solutions. The system is monitored and controlled remotely using an Android app.

articleTitle: Cryptocurrency Price Prediction Using LSTM and GRU Networks
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: cryptocurrencies are increasingly used by investors as assets, mainly for short term. Therefore, in the financial sector, prediction is important and can be done using Deep Learning techniques. This paper presents results on the prediction of three cryptocurrencies that see high volumes but are discussed in very few papers. In this paper we used LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) models and also GRU (Gated Recurrent Unit). These are applied to three important cryptocurrencies, namely DOGECoin, Ripple (XRP) and OMG Network. The results presented prove that LSTM and GRU can be successful in predicting the daily closing values for these cryptocurrencies.

articleTitle: Cubic Buck-Boost Converter with High Step-Up Capability
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The paper presents a cubic buck-boost topology that has one active switch and five diodes. Examining the static conversion ratio, it results that this converter can provide a very high step-up of the input voltage compared to the classical buck-boost and classical boost topologies. A DC analysis of the proposed converter is presented, together with its semiconductor stresses calculation. In order to prove the theoretical considerations, a simulation is performed based on the component values obtained from the design equations.

articleTitle: Performances of Uniform Sensor Array Antenna in case of DoA estimation using the MUSIC Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The resolution of a signal direction of arrival (DoA) estimation can be enhanced by an array antenna system with innovative signal processing. Super resolution algorithms take advantage of array structures to better process the incoming signals. This paper explores the eigen-analysis category of super resolution algorithm. The MUSIC (MUltiple SIgnal Classification) algorithm can be applied to estimation of the direction of arrival with a receiver formed by Uniform Linear Array (ULA) or Uniform Circular Array (UCA) antenna. In this paper, we analyze the performances obtained in both situations through computer simulation.

articleTitle: Performances Analysis of Turbo Codes, LDPC Codes and Polar Codes using AWGN channel with and without Inter Symbol Interference
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to analyse the performances of Turbo codes, LDPC (Low Density Parity Check) codes and Polar codes, over an AWGN (Additive White Gaussian Noise) channel with and without ISI (Inter Symbol Interference). In case of using an AWGN channel without ISI, the channel impulse response was considered to be unitary. In contrast, in the case of an AWGN channel in the presence of ISI, it was required to apply equalisation. In this respect, it was used Zero Forcing equalizer to remove the ISI consequences. As performance indicator the BER (Bit Error Rate) was considered for a given SNR (Signal to noise Ratio), using BPSK modulation (Binary Phase Shift Keying).

articleTitle: Analysis of Potential Threats in NextGen 5G Core
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The NextGen 5G core foundations will rely on soft-ware and programmability which are essential for the evolution of the future mobile network architecture. While the 3GPP specifications trace the key functionality between Network Functions (NFs) communication, there are many security concerns which derive from the new service deployment models against potential attacks on the main interfaces. Therefore, the protection of both signaling and user plane traffic becomes a must according to the 3GPP requirements. In this paper we simulate two use cases of attacks on the control and user plane using a traffic replay simulator dedicated to 5G Service-Based Architecture (SBA). In order to capture the behavior of NFs, we deploy the Open5GS core as microservices and we inject a service mesh solution to analyze the Access and Mobility Management Function (AMF) throughput response under the two attack scenarios.

articleTitle: The Use of Data Augmentation as a Technique for Improving Fake News Detection in the Romanian Language
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Anomalies and fake data can be identified by applying supervised learning algorithms to news sources. These techniques can help reduce the negative impact of fake news on consumers. Fake news is a widespread problem around the world and is also gaining momentum in Romania. For the detection of fake news in Romanian, we investigate methods to construct a Romanian data set and apply algorithms that offer the highest performance. To improve performance, we use a data augmentation technique called back translation in conjunction with the Support Vector Machine classifier.

articleTitle: A Real-Time Warning Based on TIAGo's Audio Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This article shows how the TIAGo service robot may be used in everyday life to help people by issuing warnings using its audio skills. This project's design aim is to create a real-time system that can track daily activities. With a total of 110 classes, the proposed database includes both dangerous and helpful sounds. Audio events detection will be processed based on a sound classification algorithm. This takes into consideration as classifier k-Nearest Neighbors (kNN), Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) while as feature extraction Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients-34 (MFCC-34) and MFCC-64. In this paper we propose an alert algorithm by email address or Short Message Service (SMS) at identification of an audio signal. The alert will be specific depending on the sound category identified. Warning based on email addresses is done in about 0.917 seconds, much faster than based on the phone number, done in about 5.912 seconds.

articleTitle: Improved Dead Reckoning Localization using IMU Sensor
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In the upcoming years, autonomous vehicle technology will advance quickly and spread widely. The most crucial component of such systems is vehicle localization or position estimation. The global navigation satellite system (GNSS) is the one of the most advanced positioning system currently in use. But the GNSS signals could be interrupted or degraded due to interference. Additionally, while GNSS delivers precise information for outdoor systems but is unable to provide a solution for indoor. An indoors-and-outdoors-usable device called an inertial measurement unit (IMU) sensor is employed in this paper to suggest a location estimate technique. The study's proposed IMU dead reckoning method makes use of novel techniques to filter noise data and accurately determine the position of the vehicle. The GNSS-based vehicle localization system can be improved by using this technique in GNSS-denied scenarios. In this paper, the IMU sensor's accelerometer, magnetometer, and gyroscope data are utilized to calculate the vehicle's velocity, orientation, and position. The experimental results on a real autonomous vehicle demonstrate that the system is effective, with average errors in rotation and translation of 1.03 degrees and 1.04 meters, respectively.

articleTitle: Cybersecurity for Embedded Systems: A review
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Encryption is the process of encoding the sensitive data so that only authorized parties or personnel can access it. Without encryption, some critical data or information would be at risk. Manufacturers and system developers are searching for better ways to protect its property using different security implementations. An embedded system need to run only authorized firmware. In this paper, we present some basic types of code protection together with a hardware based implementation that can be easily applied for an appropriate level of cybersecurity in embedded projects.

articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration of a Visible Light Communications Crosswalk Assistance System
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In the context in which pedestrians are the most exposed road user category in urban areas, this paper presents the results of an experimental demonstration of a new system designed to assist pedestrians in safely using a crosswalk. The proposed architecture consists of a pedestrian detection and localization unit that detects pedestrians in the crosswalk area, a visible light communications component that transmits this information toward the approaching vehicles using the visible light communications technology and a graphical user interface that enables the driver to receive relevant traffic safety information. The experimental investigation has shown that based on a multi-sensor data fusion approach, pedestrians are detected with an overall 100% detection rate, whereas the low power crosswalk sign VLC emitter can provide a communication range of up to 27 ― 40 meters, with a data rate of 100 kb/s and a BER in the 10–<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup>― 10–<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> range. Therefore, the experimental results indicate that the proposed VLC system has high performance in traffic situations that could pose serious issues to other concepts.

articleTitle: Human-Computer Interaction Through Voice Commands Recognition
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Despite intensive research dedicated to human machine communication, until recently only a reduced number of systems adopted vocal commands to interact with computers. With the development of deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs) architectures promising results have been obtained in speech recognition and natural language processing, allowing people to engage in simple question-answer dialog with robots. In that regard, the goal of this paper is to introduce a novel interface designed to facilitate the human-machine interaction (HMI). The framework starts by detecting and recognizing speech messages, transforming them into spoken commands. The voice controls are further converted into operating system instructions designed to automate everyday human tasks. The experimental evaluation performed on English spoken language dataset, validates the proposed architecture with average accuracy scores superior to 89%. In addition, we have compared different DCNNs architectures and identified which model has the best performance.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Online Vertical Misalignment Detection Algorithm for Automotive Radar
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper proposes a method for automatic detection and correction of the elevation mounting angle error of a 4D automotive radar integrated in a vehicle. The process requires no special calibration jig and can be used in such a way that it replaces the ordinary initial calibration methods; it also provides a continuous calibration during the lifetime of the sensor. Stationary targets reflected from the environment are used in a line fitting algorithm, for the purpose of calculating a vertical misalignment angle. The method provides a set of two correction values: a dynamic value that converges in a fast manner in case of small accidents and a more stable elevation correction value that converges slower and offers a long-term compensation value of the lifetime of the sensor. Real world data gathered from drive tests with a 77 GHz series automotive radar was used for the performance evaluation of the proposed method, showing promising results.

articleTitle: Emotion Recognition Audio Database for Service Robots
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper describes the first version of the emotional audio base for a service robot in which the sentences are in Romanian. The audio database is based on 10 sentences. Each sentence was recorded in three types of emotional states: happiness, neutral and sad, each recording being repeated 10 times. The meaning of each sentence also depends on its type of emotion. For creating the audio database, 7 people were recorded, including both female and male. For each person, 10 sentences were recorded. At this moment the database consists of 2100 audio sentences with various states of emotion. After obtaining this database, the next step would be to implement a sentence-based emotion identification algorithm for the use of service robots in various monitoring applications. In each emotional state, the average fundamental frequency for was calculated for both male and female speakers. The results indicate a significant impact of the happy emotional state upon frequency variation. The distinction between a neutral and sad emotional state is not particularly significant.

articleTitle: Urban mobility - determining the Real Catchment Area of a shop based on customer-shop interactions
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The study applies to retailers with own or franchise shops and where any customer-shop interaction is done by customer self-identification and recorded in the shop's database. The present case is specific to a mobile phone operator with access both to the information within the shops and to the signaling information of the mobile devices of its own customers.

articleTitle: Designing Applications for Collaborative Learning in Virtual Reality
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: For the past decade the virtual reality technology had a noticeable impact on many aspects of life, including education. Virtual reality has the potential to significantly support students in developing their abilities and knowledge, according to several studies cited in this paper. In fact, combining virtual reality and education can enhance learning and teaching in an interactive way. In this paper we aimed to study the impact that virtual reality adds to the education process and how important is the collaborative aspect in a virtual reality application. Consequently, we describe the design, development, and evaluation of an application for collaborative learning in virtual reality that demonstrates these approaches.

articleTitle: Kubernetes-Based Network Functions Orchestration for 5G Core Networks with Open Source MANO
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Due to the constraints imposed by the 5G requirements in terms of low latency, high availability, but also because of the need to have flexible support for business models, mobile core networks have evolved towards a cloud-native (CN) approach. This implies a whole new approach to Network Function Virtualization (NFV), ensuring an adaptation of Virtual Network Functions (VNFs) running in virtual machines (VMs). These were phased out in favor of Cloud-native Network Functions (CNFs), or Kubernetes-based Network Functions (KNFs) as they are also called in Open Source MANO (OSM) terminology. This paper discusses the KNF -based deployment of an open-source 5G core network - free5GC, using OSM and following a cloud-native approach. The experiments highlighted the advantages of choosing a containerized approach in terms of availability, obtaining an average downtime of about five times shorter (5 seconds) than in the case of virtualization (25 seconds).

articleTitle: Study of the new polymer coatings exhibiting hydrophobic / hydrophilic interactions
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In the new materials technology, conductive polymers (CP) are used to manufacture coating layers for anions and cations exchange with the base material and hydrophobic to hydrophilic interactions. A simulation strategy was developed in order to determine the contact angle (CA) of a liquid droplet on a conductive polymer layer with roughness. The analyzing method is valuable both to hydrophobic and hydrophilic polymers and illustrates the CA dependence on different parameters like roughness degree of the conductive polymer layer, droplet radius or surface tension of the fluid. The method was tested for the new CP composites reported in literature and considers the complex structure of each material variant. The illustrated dependences allow us to consider the available CP variant and its working parameters for a specific application, either a hydrophobic or a hydrophilic layer is necessary.

articleTitle: Vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser (VCSEL) based distance sensing for parking assistance
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: While VCSEL technology was first theorized in the late 70s this type of technology has seen recent growth in its presence in consumer and professional applications. The following paper analyzes the capacity of single VCSEL-based TOF (Time of flight) sensors to provide distance measurements that can be used for automotive applications, mainly to guide a driver or the vehicle during the parking process. Two VCSEL-based sensors (one for reduced range, the other for increased range) were tested to determine their real-world accuracy, filtering solutions are also presented and compared alongside an integration proposal for this type of technology in the automotive sector.

articleTitle: A Novel Hybrid Quadratic Buck Converter
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: From the step-up converter with coupled inductors, is obtained the step-down hybrid quadratic converter presented in this paper. The converter includes two coupled inductors, a separate inductor, two capacitors, three diodes, and a MOSFET transistor. The converter is analyzed considering the pair of inductors to be perfectly coupled. The main advantage of the converter is that it has two degrees of freedom, one being the duty cycle and the other one the transformer ratio. To verify theoretical results and analysis, simulations in the CASPOC software were performed, followed by practical experiments and perfect agreement was found.

articleTitle: Public Institutions Updated Enhanced Biometric Security, Zero Trust Architecture and Multi-Factor Authentification
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents the possibility of introducing multi-factor authentication using biometrics as standard practice to improve public institution cyber security. Along with the widespread implementation of such a solution, network architecture can be redesigned around a Zero Trust Architecture approach that would permit a much more granular approach to network and data security. The proposed system would also comply with current General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) standards and regulations.

articleTitle: Semantic Segmentation of Diabetic Retinopathy Imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Causing lesions on the retina, diabetic retinopathy (DR) can affect vision and lead to blindness. Although treatment exists, this can only sustain the vision if it is detected in the initial stages. Retina analysis and investigation can lead to detect several symptoms and diagnosis and to avoid complications. Image segmentation is a common task in both natural and medical image analysis. Segmentation of lesions in fundus images is essential for accurate determination of the detection of DR. The paper presents a deep leaning-based semantic segmentation of DR images using U-Net architecture, where the model uses three different pretrained networks as encoders.

articleTitle: Reinforced Hybrid Wiener Deconvolutional - Convolutional Autoencoders Based Image Deblurring
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper is addressing the issue of image deblurring by employing a novel reinforced hybrid Wiener deconvolutional-convolutional neural network (HWDCNN) in the context of images affected by Gaussian blur. The proposed method is set to explore the capabilities of a custom NN layer that performs the classical Wiener deconvolution operator in a trainable manner, hence, leading to a blind deblurring method where the weights represent the point spread functions (PSF) and signal-to-noise ratios (SNR) of the deconvolution layer which are optimized in a traditional deep learning paradigm. Additionally, the custom layer is set as a first layer on two of the branches of the model, followed by layers of transposed convolution to explore possible synergies. The results indicate that this method outperforms known state-of-the-art methods for the presented dataset setup in terms of both structural similarity index measure (SSIM) and peak SNR (PSNR) metrics.

articleTitle: FPGA Based IEEE 1451 Compliant Smart Power Supply Controller
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In comparison to the conventional microcontroller-based systems used in industrial automation, Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) becomes each year more popular as Central Processing Unit for smart devices. The lack of an operating system is an advantage in this case and separate functions can be processed individually and in the same time on one FPGA based circuit. Also it offers reduced difficulty in obtaining regulatory approvals and lessens the implementation costs. The paper approaches a method to obtain variable voltage levels with a device connected by an industrial network to a host computer. It`s structure comprises a buck converter and a Transducer Interface Module (TIM) based on a FPGA which receives commands from a Network Capable Application Processor thus making it compatible with the industrial IEEE 1451 standard specifications.

articleTitle: Network traffic logger with real-time streaming and spoofing capabilities
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Logging network traffic provides a way of keeping a close eye on the flow of data and being able to analyze it to find or troubleshoot problems as they appear. It can also aid in accessing the information the network users exchange in a way that would not be possible otherwise. Network traffic analysis can be further enhanced by adding modern technologies that allow real-time querying and pattern matching. This paper aims to showcase such a solution, specifically a network traffic logging tool that provides support for real-time network packet transfer to Apache Kafka and ksqIDB, designed to provide a fast and reliable way of storing network packets in Apache Kafka topics.

articleTitle: Man-made Noise Measurement System for HF Band Based on SDR platforms - Design and Implementation
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: HF radio communications has remained unequivocally a widely debated topic because of its advantages in providing not only communications over distances of up to thousands of kilometers, but also because of its applicability in a wide range of applications. However, for the most reliable communications planning, knowledge of the electromagnetic environment in general and radio noise in particular is essential. Radio noise affects the receiving system either from natural external sources or from unintentional radiation. This paper approaches these unintentional sources, also known as man-made noise, with a focus on one of its dominant components, namely White Gaussian Noise. Accordingly, for the measurement of Gaussian noise we propose a measurement system based on SDR platforms, characterized by its flexibility in configuration. The system also includes a Rohde&Schwarz HFH2-Z6E broadband active rod antenna connected to an R&S®IN600 Bias unit. The purpose of this paper is to design, implement and test this system to measure WGN noise, for the frequency range 2-12MHz using the “20% method”, expressed in standardized dB at a bandwidth of 1 Hz.

articleTitle: Combined Engineered Cells For Multiband, Wide Band, And Miniaturized Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This work considers an antenna's electromagnetic (EM) response toward two combined cells outlining the electromagnetic band gap (EBG) structures. It has been demonstrated that EBG structures either act as a high impedance surface (HIS) or as an artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) that usually assist in achieving different functions. In this paper, the standard mushroom-like cells are combined with either EBG-CS or EBG-CSML cells (which are deeply explored previously). They are arranged in three periodic manners (Chessboard-like, Intervallic-like, and Mirror-like). The aim is to study the EM features of these EBG structures when integrated with antennas. The motivation behind this work is to bring out the eventual ability of any of those periodic configurations under test, either to obtain multiband antennas with competitive performances or to reach wide bandwidth resonating systems. The result shows a very interesting performance of the Intervallic structure when integrated with our printed dipole antenna (PDA), which manifests in wide bandwidth equal to 0.6 GHz at 3.2 GHz (the realized fractional bandwidth FBW is equal to 20%) and an additional band around 5 GHz. The presented EBG antenna is designed for the purpose of making a new competitive compact and miniaturized multiband antenna, as the central frequency was shifted from 4.6 GHz (PDA in free space) to 3.2 GHz (PDA with the Intervallic architecture). The result is validated by simulating the 73 Ohm half-wave dipole antenna (HWDA) with the proposed configuration, the result is agreeable. This system could be resized to work around mobile's 5G low and mid bands (0.7 GHz-2.6 GHz) to make attractive and competitive tiny antennas.

articleTitle: Robotic Arm Control via Hand Movements
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The paper presents the construction of a robotic arm controlled using basic human hand movements. The glove assembly contains three flexible sensors and two accelerometers on the transceiver side. The glove contains an Arduino N ano to control the stepper motor and six servo-motors, and the robotic arm contains an Arduino Uno, six servo-motors and a stepper motor. The glove has three 3D-printed fingers. Each finger has three degrees of freedom and is controlled by a human hand. The hand-controlled robotic arm can be useful in various industries such as medical, chemical and military.

articleTitle: Evaluating Research Trends Using Key Term Occurrences and Multivariate Mann-Kendall Test
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper offers a quantifiable means for assessing the trend in the interest of scientific community in a particular research theme. Representing the research theme as a set of key terms, we investigate its trend within the scientific literature, using a corpus of paper metadata belonging to flagship journals and conferences that are relevant for the encompassing domain. Our method employs a multivariate version of the Mann-Kendall test that is applied to a multivariate time series of key term occurrences in order to discover if the trend of the research theme is ascending, descending or if there is no monotonic trend. Finally, an illustrative case study, examining the effectiveness of the proposed method for three research themes from Electronic Design Automation field, is presented.

articleTitle: Radial Basis Functions Neural Network on Microcontrollers
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents an implementation of a neural network based on radial functions and evaluates its performance using general purpose microcontrollers. As an example, an application of EGC signal classification based on the wavelet transform is presented. The evaluation of the implementation considers the number of clusters in which the inputs are divided, and the type of wavelet transformation used. The main results indicate that the implementation of a neural network based on radial functions is possible in real time (testing phase) with very good classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Multi-Core Time-Triggered OCBP-Based Scheduling for Mixed Criticality Periodic Task Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of real-time scheduling on multiprocessor platforms for periodic tasks in a time-triggered mixed criticality environment. A partitioned, non-preemptive, table-driven scheduling algorithm was proposed, called Partitioned Time-Triggered Own Criticality Based Priority (P-TT -OCBP), based on a uniprocessor mixed criticality method. Furthermore, an analysis of the scheduling algorithm is provided in terms of success ratio by comparing it against an event-driven and a time-triggered method.

articleTitle: Medium-Term Forecasting of Global Horizontal Solar Radiation in Brasov Using Multivariate Transformer
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In solar radiation forecasting, changes in a variable such as diffused horizontal solar radiation, temperature, sunny days, and time may provide important details about global horizontal solar radiation behavior. Thus, multivariate global solar radiation forecasting is more attractive in renewable energy integration into the electric grid. With this motivation, we devoted this paper to propose a multivariate transformer-based forecasting model for global solar radiation forecasting. The proposed transformer-based global solar radiation forecasting model effectiveness was validated with the comparative investigation. The proposed multivariate Transformer forecasting model obtained an MSE of 0.3422. The prior existing forecasting models such as persistent, numerical weather prediction (NWP), Autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA), Backpropagation Network (BPN), Support Vector Machines (SVM), Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), Elman Neural Network (ENN), Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) based forecasting of global solar radiation is lack behind the multivariate transformer based forecasting in term of accuracy and convergence for the medium-term horizon based forecasting. Hence, the proposed forecasting model proves that it surpasses the prior forecasting model and aids in power system planning and energy marketing.

articleTitle: Open-Source Software-Defined Wide Area Network: An Inter-Cloud Approach
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents an open-source solution for Software-Defined Wide Area Network (SD-WAN). The data plane included two Mininet virtual machines (VMs) on Ubuntu 18.04 LTS, each on a distinct physical machine and in different networks. Within the first one, three instances of Open vSwitch (OVS) were used to provide high network availability. Similarly, the second Mininet also had three such switches to enable the Local Area Network (LAN) communication. The flow tables of each OVS were updated by the SD-WAN controller using OpenFlow 1.4. The inter-networking was facilitated by a full-mesh of Generic Routing Encapsulation (GRE) tunnels backed-up by another full-mesh of Virtual eXtensible Local Area Network (VXLAN) overlay networks. The control plane was represented by a cluster of two ONOS 2.5.0 Docker containerized instances to further increase the availability. Another cluster of Atomix containers acted as a storage element and enabled the ONOS containers to work together as a coherent group. Each Mininet emulated two hosts in order to evaluate the inter-cloud performance using the following scenarios: (1) seamless connectivity; (2) effective data rate and Round-Trip Time (RTT) comparison between GRE and VXLAN tunnels.

articleTitle: Using a Radio Remote Controller to Operate a Rover and Robotic Arm Combo
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents the creation and control of a rover and robotic arm combo, or in other words terrestrial drone. The terrestrial drone can be used for getting in places, where the human beings don't have access. It can be used in space explorations, bomb disarming, narrow spaces, radioactive fields, surveillance and others. The control of the whole system is done with a radio remote controller, to ease the process. The whole system is made out a rover and robotic arm, so the systems has 9 motors to control (4 motors for the rover and 5 motors for the robotic arm).

articleTitle: Real-Time Monitoring and Command System for the Cheia Space Surveillance and Tracking Radar
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The monitoring of space objects and debris in various orbits around Earth is of high importance for human activity in space, due to increasing risks to satellites and other spacecraft, but also due to the potential threat to people and assets on the ground. The European Space Policy for years 2021–2027 acknowledges and deals with this problem, includes a dedicated element for Space Situational Awareness (SSA) and requires the establishment of a Framework for Space Surveillance and Tracking (EUSST) Support. As part of this effort, a new space tracking sensor, the CHEIA SST Radar, is being developed and installed in Romania with the purpose of being included in the EUSST sensors network and of contributing to the joint database of space objects orbiting the Earth. The paper describes the Monitoring and Command System of this Radar and describes the processes of design, simulation, and implementation of the software building blocks that make up this important radar sub-system.

articleTitle: Preliminary Results on Contrast Enhanced Ultrasound Video Stream Diagnosis Using Deep Neural Architectures
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In recent years, the interest in the deep learning (DL) paradigm has grown dramatically. Due to its ability to automatically extract characteristics and recognize patterns from data, this technology has been particularly successful in the field of medical imaging. The current paper proposes a fully automatic computer-aided diagnosis DL-based system for the investigation of contrast enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) video streams in order to identify specific focal liver lesions (FLL). Our solution, based on a combination of a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a recurrent neural network (RNN) showed promising results (87% accuracy) when it was evaluated against the SYSU dataset.

articleTitle: Urban landmark detection using A-KAZE features and vector of aggregated local descriptors
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Urban landmarks detection systems represent a research topic that is continuously pursued in the Computer Vision domain. These systems play an important role in tourism and cultural heritage storytelling augmented reality applications in urban environments. In this paper, we propose a system that aims to recognize landmarks from urban scenarios using A-KAZE features and aggregated local descriptors. The proposed system was evaluated on popular public datasets like ZuBuD and TMBuD obtaining positive results.

articleTitle: Control Method for Multiphase DC-DC Converter in Drive Train of Fuel Cell Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In the framework of the European Union (EU) SWARM project, a fuel cell vehicle fleet has been built. As a result, a multiphase DC-DC converter has been developed with a special control method to be installed between the battery and the fuel cell in these vehicles driving trains. In order to prove the control methodology, a test platform has been built, which consists of a fuel cell system, a DC-DC converter, a battery pack, and an electronic load. The paper proposes and verifies a procedure for controlling the fuel cell system output and validates it on the test platform that was practically realized.

articleTitle: Grouping farmers using agglomerative clustering on data generated from statistics
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The creation of agricultural clusters is one of the methods by which farmers can increase their competitiveness and generate economic growth. Machine learning can help to decide which are the best clusters to form in an area. The aim of the paper is to examine the possibility of using clustering on an agricultural platform. This platform is under development, and currently there are no real data available for training purposes. Therefore, we constructed a data set by integrating multiple data sources. This was constructed to be as similar as possible to the characteristics of the data available in the final platform. The proposed data set consists of 4480 records and 60 features, ranging from geographical location to crop yield. Next, the experimental part proposes a scenario for grouping the farmers based on geographic proximity and crop yield.

articleTitle: TV News Database Indexing System with Video Structure Analysis, Representative Images Extractions and OCR for News Titles
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In this paper, we present the semiautomatic system for analysis of the temporal structure of a news show, where the indexing of TV news program material is done following a classification resulting from the segmentation of video sequences, the definition of areas of interest and the recognition of news titles through automatic optical text recognition. Several experiments are presented regarding video segmentation methods, text extraction methods, and models of temporal and spatial structures that define a TV news program.

articleTitle: Preliminary investigation of dye-sensitized solar cells for an optoelectronic neural network with zero electric power consumption
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The transformative potential of artificial intelligence (AI) to contribute to the achievement of a green transition, especially in a sustainable development of urban areas, the “smart city”, has been increasingly and prominently highlighted. At the same time, digital technologies, such as AI, significantly increase energy and resource consumption and create risks of adverse environmental effects. In this context, solar cells offer a new perspective as the most suitable candidate for zero electric power consumption. The dye-sensitized solar cell (DSSC) has the essential characteristics that could make these cells an ideal candidate for an artificial intelligence system with zero electric power consumption. This new perspective for AI devices, which are the optically learning solar cells, have the potential to serve as building blocks for intelligent optoelectronics enabling visually interacting machines that operate at minimal power and zero electric power consumption, in both outdoor and indoor lighting conditions. Here, we report a preliminary demonstration that dye-sensitized solar cells loaded with ultraviolet (UV) dye and visible (Vis) dye could learn using illumination time as a cue.

articleTitle: A Brief Overview on 3D Perception using Deep Neural Networks for Automotive
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Technologies in automotive industry have been improved very much in the last few years. Since technology enhances our daily activity, many automotive companies are looking for implementing different features for cars to make our life easier. One of the most advanced capabilities is represented by autonomous driving. This task typically implies intensive 3D perception of the environment. Perception involves the collection of the data coming from sensors which are considered to be relevant for learning the environment. The aim of the current paper is to review the point cloud-based 3D object perception using deep neural networks works with application in automotive. The study refers to the whole problematic associated with this challenging task, including the necessary hardware for acquiring the 3D data, the publicly available point cloud datasets and the deep neural network models which are able to process point cloud data.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Dynamic Performance of an USB Oscilloscope
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In this paper the dynamic performance of an USB oscilloscope is determined through the Effective Number Of Bits (ENOB) and the baseline noise parameters. The ENOB parameter is estimated by means of the three-parameter sine-fit algorithm. The analysis is performed at different frequencies in two operation modes: normal and resolution enhancement. The latter mode is used to increase the oscilloscope vertical resolution. Moreover, the dynamic performance of the analyzed USB oscilloscope is compared with that of a benchtop Digital Storage Oscilloscope (DSO) by means of the above parameters.

articleTitle: An Optimal Implementation of an 8b/10b Encoder for Xilinx FPGAs
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: We propose an optimal structural design of an 8b/10b encoder for Xilinx FPGAs. The proposed approach aims at reducing the number of look-up tables used for the implementation. We compare our design with two state-of-the-art solutions and two behavioral models. The implementation results show that our solution provides the lowest resource utilization, logic delay and power consumption.

articleTitle: Sandbox Integrated Gateway for the Discovery of Cybersecurity Vulnerabilities
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Emails are widely used as a form of communication and sharing files in an organization. However, email is widely used by cybercriminals to spread malware and carrying out cyber-attacks. We implemented an open-source email gateway in conjunction with a security sandbox for securing emails against malicious attachments. The email gateway scans all incoming and outgoing emails and stops emails containing suspicious files. An automated python script would then send the suspected email to the sandboxing element through sandbox API for further analysis, while the script is used also for the prevention of duplicate results. Moreover, the mail server administrator receives notifications from the email gateway about suspicious attachments. If detected attachment is a true positive based on the sandbox analysis result, email is deleted, otherwise, the email is delivered to the recipient. The paper describes in an empirical way the steps followed during the implementation, results, and conclusions of our research.

articleTitle: Congestion Study of Transport Layer in DL 5G Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Fifth generation (5G) radio systems represent a predictable evolution of the mobile network to achieve new capabilities. As the previous generation, 5G mobile networks will provide high data rate connectivity for smartphones, tablets, and IoT as well. 5G takes the traditional mobile broadband to the extreme in terms of data rates, capacity, spectrum efficiency and availability. For these targets, 5G requires various protocols to support its multiples features, such as Transmission Control Protocol (TCP), which provides high-speed data rates. In this paper we analyze the performances of TCP on top of File Transfer Protocol (FTP) model 2. User throughput, total cell throughput, Round Trip Time (RTT), delay and Physical Resource Block (PRB) utilization are the analyzed metrics for FTP protocol.

articleTitle: Experimental Determination of the Area Coverage of a TETRA Base Station in a Dense Urban Area
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents the determination of the area coverage for a TETRA base station located in the center of a city from Romania. The characterization of the area coverage involved making some measurements to determine the power level for a TETRA radio channel. Low-cost platforms such as Raspberry Pi and Adalm Pluto were used to make these measurements. The system responsible for measuring the power level runs on the Raspberry Pi platform and was built using the GNU Radio software application. The system runs independently and can be configured to be mobile. The built system can be used to make various measurements that can be compared with simulations.

articleTitle: Prediction of Machine Temperature System Failure Using a Novel Activation Function
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper aims to validate activation function capabilities to bring improvement regarding predictions. Using an activation function that we developed in our previous work, a composed function, we extend it with experiments into timeseries data, having as its focus activation function behavior compared to existing activation functions, the purpose being to introduce a more suitable alternative that's capable of improvements and a smoother variation during training, offering fast convergence. In addition, we compare our proposal with other popular functions such as Sigmoid, Rectified Linear Unit, and Swish. Furthermore, the proposed composed activation function is shown to accelerate the minimization process of the loss values in deep learning using a time-series machine temperature system failure dataset.

articleTitle: Speech Emotion Recognition Using 1D/2D Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Over the last few decades, emotion recognition has been a hot topic of research in the affective computing community. The automatic identification of emotions from raw speech signals is highly challenging and depends on multiple factors, including: the utterance length, the speaker language, gender or accent. In addition, the process is highly subjective because people can perceive emotions differently. In that regard, the goal of this paper is to evaluate some state-of-the-art deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs) architectures receiving as input various ID/2D speech feature representations, conduct experiments on a publicly available dataset (Ryerson Audio-Visual Database of Emotional Speech and Song Dataset - RA VDESS) and identify which architecture has the best performance in the discrete emotion classification task.

articleTitle: Sound Encryption using Wavelet Transform and Composite Chaotic Function
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper proposes an encryption algorithm for speech signals based on the discrete wavelet transform and a new chaotic map composed by three chaotic systems: Sine-Cubic-Tent chaotic map. The results of the encryption with the composite chaotic map are compared with the results obtained with each chaotic system. The metrics obtained with this new chaotic map are very good in terms of robustness and speed.

articleTitle: Predictive Analytics Models for Student Admission to Master Programs in Romania
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This study examines the student admission process at Politehnica University Timisoara's Faculty of Electronics, Telecommunications, and Information Technologies for master's engineering programs. The focus of the study is the student's admission prediction into the mainstream programs offered by our faculty. The programs in this category are the most successful and stable. Most of the features we use have been geared toward the options of future degree programs students may choose to pursue. In these experiments, we used several evaluation methods, including stratified cross-validation and evaluation of unseen data chunks that were not used for training. The Gradient Boost Classifier performs the best of the six models. Among the conclusions drawn is that secondary options do not provide relevant information for predictive models. We implemented the experiments using a low-code framework; as a result, the predictive analysis pipeline was largely automated.

articleTitle: Instrumentation and Analyzis of Handover in Wi-Fi Networks
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Mobility is an important characteristic of pervasive communication today, providing users with mobility while keeping existing connections. This requirement is possible by transferring moving users from one access point to another, process called handover. This paper describes the measurement and instrumentation setup proposed to analyze the handover process in controller based Wi-Fi networks. Experimental results on the latency and QoS impact of different applications during the handover in an IEEE 802.11a/b/g/n network, are also provided.

articleTitle: A Horn Antenna Array Design for the Ku band
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Modern wireless communication systems require high gain and high bandwidth antennas which are able to provide better performance. This paper presents the design and simulation of a broadband pyramidal horn antenna array for satellite applications. First, a pyramidal horn antenna with a single optimized element is designed, and then the optimization of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 1$</tex> array is done using different distances between the elements of the array to obtain a high gain. The horn antenna array is excited through a power splitter circuit and an impedance matching circuit. The final antenna array provides a gain of 24.5 dBi at a resonant frequency of 13.3 GHz. The simulation results show a low voltage standing wave ratio, a good radiation of the Ku-band model and a high gain compared to a single horn antenna. The simulations were performed with the ANSYS HFSS program. The proposed antenna array operates in the Ku frequency band.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Mini-Panel and Thermoelectric Generator Under Concentrated Light
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The increase in efficiency of photovoltaic cells and panels is a very ambitious target. One way to achieve it is by using hybridization with thermoelectric generators, either thermally connected or not. This paper presents an experimental system with an amorphous photovoltaic mini-panel and a thermoelectric generator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{Bi}_{2}\mathbf{Te_3}$</tex>, not thermally connected, with beam splitter and the results in two functioning regimes: steady-state and transient regime using concentrated light from the sun and from xenon lamps. The behavior analysis of the hybrid system with beam splitter shows that the amorphous photovoltaic mini-panel can be used at a concentration ratio of up to 50.

articleTitle: A New Slight Step-Up Quadratic Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: A novel single-switch quadratic boost converter is presented in this paper. Its static conversion ratio indicates that the proposed topology is well suited in applications requiring a slight step-up of the input voltage compared to the classical boost. Static characteristics are derived and the semiconductor stresses proved to be lower than in the classical boost. For the considered design example, a measured efficiency of 93% was obtained. According to the design relationships, a prototype was breadboarded. First the designed converter was simulated, then subjected to practical experiments. Finally, the theoretical aspects were confirmed by the simulations and the experimental results, thus proving the feasibility of the proposed converter.

articleTitle: Low-cost GNSS Monitoring Station for Raw Data Measurements
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents the development and implementation of a GNSS monitoring system using low-cost solutions. The system is autonomous and can be configured and controlled remotely through an Internet connection. The system will be used to make raw data measurements that will be used to determine the carrier-to-noise density, the pseudorange, and other important parameters of the satellites in each constellation of the Global Navigation Satellite System. The system consists of a Raspberry Pi 4 with 8 Gb RAM, a GNSS sensor model U-blox ZED-F9P, GNSS antenna model Taoglas A80, Huawei 4G modem model E3372 and power bank with solar charge.

articleTitle: A Decomposition-Based RLS Algorithm for Stereophonic Acoustic Echo Cancellation
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In hands-free teleconferencing systems, stereo transmission provides telepresence thanks to our binaural hearing system and gives a realistic presence that actual single-channel systems cannot offer. In this context, stereophonic acoustic echo cancellation (SAEC) is necessary for full-duplex quality communication. Nevertheless, the long length of the acoustic impulse responses represents one of the main challenges in SAEC, which significantly impacts the overall performance of the adaptive filters used to model the acoustic echo paths. In this paper, we propose a decomposition-based approach using the nearest Kronecker product, which results in a combination of shorter filters to solve the original system identification problem. The solution is formulated in terms of the recursive least-squares (RLS) algorithm, which is very appealing for its convergence features. Besides the lower computational complexity, the proposed decomposition-based RLS algorithm achieves a better tracking behavior as compared to its conventional counterpart. Simulation results support these practical features.

articleTitle: Software Optimization used to Automate Decellularization
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In the field of tissue engineering, obtaining biomatrices raises serious problems, both for the physician and the biomedical engineer. Until now, there is no standardized and very well optimized decellularization protocol. All applied and used protocols allow for an advanced degree of decellularization, but they also generally produce some damage, which affects the quality of the future organ to be transplanted. In this study, we present the optimization of the software application created for the automatic validation of the decellularization process for a simulated heart. Thus, the heart was simulated using a latex balloon, in which dye was inserted. It was distilled, injecting water with a controlled flow, using a syringe pump for clinical use so that the software application automatically detects, after a long time, the complete discolouration of the simulated heart and automatically stops the process. Finally, this process is equivalent to the complete decellularization of a real heart. The validation of the optimization of the software application was made using the spectrophotometric measurement of the evolution of the dye concentration used in this experimental process.

articleTitle: RISC-V based HW accelerator
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper deals with implementation of an example of implementation of an algorithm into an FPGA. While some considerations about various possibilities (ASIC, ASIP, GPP) are made, here is demonstrated the ASIP version with implementation details. An economic version of a Reed-Solomon algorithm is demonstrated and further developments of the method are assessed.

articleTitle: Checking Over the Separation Performance for Winner Take All in Subthreshold Regime
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The Lazzaro basic WTA in weak inversion is considered for numerical checking of winner-loser gap in the output list. The technological mismatch is also addressed.

articleTitle: The temporal imprint of mobile phone emission level when running various applications in 4G versus 5G networks
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Human exposure to electromagnetic fields emitted by mobile communications sources is dominated by the mobile phone radiation. Not only the dose of radiation is important, but also dose- or fluence-rate. In this regard, present research emphasizes the features of the dynamics of mobile terminal emission levels by means of statistics, nonlinear data analysis with recurrence quantification and time-frequency analyses. Time series of radiated electric field strengths were recorded and processed for a set of five mobile applications usage per communication standard. Both 4G-LTE emission channel of 20 MHz bandwidth and 5G-NR FR1 emission channel with a bandwidth of 40 MHz were studied. Differences between 4G and 5G emissions variabilities are presented, and application-specific features of the time imprint are highlighted.

articleTitle: Design of All Dielectric Frequency Selective Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Several all-dielectric surfaces are introduced in this paper aiming to obtain various stop bands between 6 and 12 GHz, and also demonstrating that filtering in the X band (8–12 GHz) can be achieved without the use of metallic structures. Properties of the structures have been assessed by full-wave simulation. The parametric analyses included in the research also showed that changing the geometrical parameters enabled the control of the working frequency. The performance of the proposed structures has been assessed through the reflection coefficient, whilst also dielectric resonator theory (interpretation of effective permittivity and permeability) has been approached to explain the operation of the proposed structures.

articleTitle: Analysis of web traffic using MPLS technology
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Multi-Protocol Label Switching provides a simplification and a substantial increase in the speed of the packet routing process in IP networks. This is done through optimization processes prior to the routing process. In the case of optical communications, there are a few problems with the routing of IP requests, which creates a large space for optimizations. This paper is a study on web traffic using MPLS technology.

articleTitle: TEM Cell Measurements in Automotive EMC: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: TEM (Transverse Electromagnetic) Cell is a device for generating a broadband standard electric field and measuring radiation power. This work takes a pragmatic approach and presents a verification procedure and a measuring setup for a TEM cell. The test procedure complies with ISO 11452–3. The test setup is based on measured data from various TEM cell scenarios that were run to see which one would work best for the specific application. Our main focus has been to present the challenges that appear with the implementation of this new test method in the EMC Laboratory.

articleTitle: Automatic Waste Segregation System
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents an automatic waste segregation system. The system is able to detect waste autonomously and separate it accurately by using a deep neural network for waste recognition. With waste recognition and automatic navigation functions, the system can efficiently and autonomously clean waste on the ground in places like parks or schools. The hardware architecture of the system includes a module Raspberry Pi, a webcam, PIC microcontrollers, EEPROM memory, a DC motor, a pick and place robotic arm, infrared and ultrasound sensors, a gyroscope, and GPS sensors. From the software point of view, the main parts are represented by the object detection module and a classification algorithm based on convolutional neural network architecture. This system would help in the easy recovery of recyclable items.

articleTitle: Exploring Educational Scenarios through Interactive Environments and Agile User Stories: a Gamified Assessment Case Study
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Emerging technologies and methods in educational activities have been developed with the aim of making the learning process more effective and engaging. In such a context, the current work proposes an educational assessment scenario through a 3D agile graphic environment. Elements of a Car Racing game (points, progress bar, check points) have been used to develop an interactive assessment environment, where the navigation architecture adapts the Agile Scrum framework, as an alternative mean to promote assessment achievements, aiming at reducing the cognitive stress present in traditional educational evaluation scenarios. (Abstract)

articleTitle: Novel methods for measuring the shutter speed of film cameras using image processing
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In photography, there are three exposure parameters: the shutter speed, the aperture, and the film sensitivity (ISO). In modern cameras, the camera body is responsible for setting the shutter speed (i.e., exposure time) and the ISO, while film cameras set only the shutter speed, therefore it is their main performance parameter. The shutter mechanism in most film cameras is mechanical, involving the use of springs. The springs wear in time, leading to losing the calibration of the shutter speed, thus the exposure time becomes longer than the designed value. The accurate measurement of the shutter speed is thus a very important performance evaluation process that allows a proper estimation of the camera's market value. This paper presents two innovative methods that allows the precise measurement of a camera's shutter speed using image processing. They involve the recording of the mechanical shutter during the exposure process using a high-speed camera, then applying the corresponding image processing algorithm on each of the recorded frames to automatically determine the exposure time. The paper presents the experimental setup, the image processing algorithms and the results obtained during testing.

articleTitle: A New VLSI Algorithm for a VLSI Implementation of MDST using Obfuscation Technique
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In this paper we present a new VLSI algorithm for an efficient VLSI implementation of the Modified Discrete Sine Transform (MDST) using the systolic array architectural paradigm. The new algorithm decomposes the computation of the MDST into two modular and regular computational structures called pseudo-cycle convolution that have the same form. This can be exploited to significantly reduce the hardware complexity since the two computational structures can be computed on the same linear systolic array using interleaving. The obtained VLSI architecture has all the advantages of a pseudo-cycle convolution based systolic implementation, such as high-speed using concurrency, an efficient use of the VLSI technology due to its local and regular interconnection topology and low I/O cost. Moreover, a cost-effective application of an obfuscation technique can be achieved with low overheads.

articleTitle: BLE Network Sensors with IoT Capability
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents a Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) network sensors. The sensor nodes of the network are based on a CC2541 microcontroller and play the role of the server. The network also contains a client that is designed around an ESP32 microcontroller. The client collects data from all sensor nodes and presents it on a local display. Furthermore, the ESP32 is connected to the internet using its Wi-Fi capability. In this way the sensor data can be accessed from everywhere by means of a smartphone with internet access. Experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: Simulation of Inverted F-type Antenna Arrays for Evaluation of Bluetooth Connectivity between a wBMU and wCMUs for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: According to the 2020 report from Global Electric Vehicle Outlook [1], it is estimated that by 2030, almost 30 % of all new vehicle fleet will be based on electric propulsion. Thus, there is an imperious need to push forward the technical improvements in the E-mobility domain. As presented in [2], there are several important gains obtained, by shifting from a dedicated wired communication protocol to a wireless antenna-based system, with regards to battery monitoring. They are represented by the exclusion of cables and connectors so that the bill of materials can be reduced, as fewer components are needed; the increase of energy density by reducing the space required for cables & connectors; the flexibility in adaptation of modules and the diminishing of recall/ repair time intervals as fewer cable connections are present in the battery pack. The following paper aims to present a methodology for investigating the operation of antenna arrays incorporated in an EV battery pack. The possible challenges when it comes to integrating a wireless communication system within a Battery Management Unit (BMU) stand for the potential disturbances to the wireless network from external electro-magnetic sources. The Cell Monitoring Circuits (CMUs) will be used for monitoring the electric and thermal parameters of the battery cells for a non-commercial battery pack. An investigation is highlighted regarding the electromagnetic coupling efficiency of Inverted F-type Antennas (IFAs) used for both the BMU and CMU modules. Starting from a general IFA topology, the antenna scattering parameters, radiation efficiency and matching circuit will be computed by using a three-dimensional FEM simulation tool. The calculus will be performed in order to simulate the operating conditions for a frequency bandwidth of 2.4 up to 2.4835 GHz. A frequency sweep will be carried out to evaluate how the IFAs behave outside the desired frequency spectrum. Simulations will be carried out to highlight the behavior at both a component level for the master and slave radio-frequency units, but also at a system level for multiple modules placed in a battery pack enclosed by a metal housing.

Author Keywords: Resonance Frequency and Finite Element Method

articleTitle: Digital Control Method for Power Electronics Converters Simulation: Application to a Front-End Single-Active Bridge AC/DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents a generalizable method to design a simulation model of a digital control for power electronic converters with the objective to optimize computational costs. The final motivation of this research is to study the possibility of using Low-voltage Direct Current in energy distribution for future applications of domestic and commercial grids for efficiency purposes. The present analysis is focused on taking into consideration the influence of a digital control in the simulation of a power electronics converter, without the need of Hardware-In-The-Loop techniques, which can be expensive, with the objective of finding an optimal computational engine. The proposed method uses the Tustin transform approximation to create discrete control laws from their continuous counterparts. To demonstrate its interest and performance, the method is applied in the control of a front-end single-active bridge AC/DC converter using PLECS software to build the simulation models.

articleTitle: Outdoor Image Segmentation based on Light Polarization Signatures
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Semantic image segmentation is an important step in scene understanding and is used in many applications, like computer vision, remote sensing, precision agriculture, autonomous driving etc. We propose a new handcrafted image segmentation algorithm based on light polarization pixel signatures, by acquiring images with a circular polarization filter rotated by 360° (in steps of 10°). We use the spectral angle mapper (SAM) to compare the polarization signatures of neighbor pixels and then, with the SAM values we construct three standard deviation image planes in a multi-resolution approach. The K-means clustering is used for the final segmentation, being applied on a 7-plane feature image. The results are compared with the classic K-means clustering and with the SegNet neural network using several quality metrics.

articleTitle: State of the Art Recognition of Emotions from Speech, Using a Low Complexity Solution Based on Reaction-Diffusion Transform
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: A low complexity solution for the problem of emotional speech recognition is provided and evaluated demonstrating state of the art accuracies for relevant emotional speech databases. The relevance of proper augmentation in the sound domain is demonstrated, with important increases in accuracies. In comparison to more traditional methods based on mel-cepstral coefficients or recurrent layers, our method offers a simpler way to compute spectrograms and consequently would reduce the complexity of the implementation, for instance the proposed method was recently implemented in a mobile platform (running autonomously from any network connectivity). Test accuracy of 96.83 % is obtained for the EMO-Db dataset and 96.63% for the RAVDESS datasets.

articleTitle: A Step-Down Hybrid Converter With Unequal Inductor
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: A step-down topology derived from a hybrid converter is presented. The converter contains only two inductors, the output capacitor and one transistor. The operation is analyzed assuming unequal inductors and the main equations are provided. It is shown that the static conversion ratio it is not affected by the fact that the inductors have different values. The simulation results accompanied by the practical experiments they all confirmed the validity of the theoretical considerations.

articleTitle: Image Denoising Using the Hurst Exponent: A Fusion Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: We propose in this paper a denoising method based on the texture roughness appreciation, realized using a semi-local estimation of the Hurst exponent. The estimation is made in the Dual Tree Complex Wavelet domain, by using techniques such as the least squares or the lasso. The Hurst exponent is used to correct the energy distribution of the wavelet coefficients. This removes the noise in homogeneous areas but can oversmooth the edges. In order to overcome this, we propose a fusion based approach, based on the observation that the noise is less visible on the edges. Both the denoised image as well as the original image are weighted by images that depend on the Hurst parameter, such that the edges are less degraded, and the correction is applied predominantly in the homogeneous areas. Our simulation results are promising for images containing both smooth areas as well as edges for the fusion based approach.

articleTitle: Distribution Of Renewable Energy In Light-Rail Traction Grids
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Electric powered Light-Rail is considered as a green sustainable alternative for public transport in highly dense populated areas. However, in the electrical-energy-transition, the power source should be renewable. Solar farms, and solar modules on public buildings in the inner city, could be this renewable source. Traction overhead lines, are used for only 20% of their capacity. Therefore it is proposed, to use the traction overhead lines as a DC grid, for the distribution of the renewable energy. Renewable energy from solar farms and city facades, is transported via the traction overhead lines into the inner city center. The concept of controlled distribution through traction overhead lines is discussed and demonstrated.

articleTitle: A Kalman Filter for the Identification of Impulse Responses with Particular Symmetry Features
