publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The identification of long-length impulse responses raises challenging issues in the context of many important applications. In this paper, we consider a theoretical model of the system to be identified, which consists in a combination of bilinear forms that owns particular symmetry features. Following a decomposition of the global impulse response using the Kro-necker product, the conventional system identification problem can be solved based on a combination of the estimates provided by two shorter filters. The solution is formulated in terms of a Kalman filter, with lower computational complexity and improved performance, as compared to the conventional approach. Simulation results outline the advantages of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Hyperspectral Image Classification using Extended Local Binary Patterns and Wavelet Transform Descriptors
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The performance and accuracy of the hyperspectral image classifier depends on the specific features present in the image as well as the method employed to select the samples used for the learning stage. In this paper, we investigate the use of evolved texture descriptors in a spectral-spatial design for the classification of hyperspectral images. We integrate the Extended Local Binary Pattern operator in a parallel hyperspectral image classification framework chain that uses wavelet descriptors for the spectral dimension. We investigate the benefits of the rich spatial information on the accuracy obtained based on the classification chain, and we show through experimental validation carried out on two open datasets (Salinas and Pavia University) that the performances are improved. The proposed framework with the corresponding methods performs well when evaluated on the two open datasets, by using a random, respectively controlled strategy for selecting the databases for training and testing.

articleTitle: The poly-alphabetic substitution ciphers - a viable solution for IoT applications?
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Trying to answer to a simple question, with a rather complicated answer, as “are poly-alphabetic substitution ciphers a viable solution for IoT?”, this work approaches the domain of symmetric cryptography through two poly-alphabetic encryption algorithms - Vigenere's and Baptista's. The former, from classical cryptography, the latter from chaos-based enciphering domain. Text and image have been subject to encryption using both methods in MATLAB simulation and their performances were compared. They proved to be similar and weaker when opposed to a third algorithm from the literature, when applied to the same data from two frequently used databases. A basic analysis of the 802.14.5 technical standard used in the Internet of Things (IoT) private-key cryptography-based security is investigated. Furthermore, the same statistical attack utilizing the coincidence index and the Chi-Squared test proven efficient on Vigenère's cipher is advanced as a possible valid cryptanalysis for all poly-alphabetic substitutions, including Baptista's cryptographic system and IoT's Advanced Encryption Standard (AES).

articleTitle: Human individuals' localization monitoring (using open source technologies)
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Remote human beings location monitoring through methods that are provided remotely managed open source services, becomes a required component in many public and private systems that work with human beings and for theirs benefits (in this category can also be included citizens with a certain degree of disability, or having limited movement areas).

articleTitle: Cyberloafing - A Major Influencer To Online Learning
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: E-learning is a dynamically changing process of learning and training in educational settings, corporate sectors and at individual or personal levels. Information communication technologies (ICT) enable support for distance learning, and the role of innovative technologies in learning tends to increase the level of knowledge and competencies of learners of different levels. However, disruption enabled by such technologies has severe impacts on learning outcomes of learners. This study presents a review of recent trends in technologies and provides a review of the recently published articles. The study also looks at common challenges, and highlights Cyberloafing as a major challenge to present online e-learning systems. The results of a survey conducted indicate that Cyberloafing is an increasing trend among learners. Therefore, the study presents possible recommendations to avoid Cyberloafing in educational settings and gives a perspective of future directions in the area of E-learning.

articleTitle: Normalized Cross Correlation based Solution for Automated Optical Inspection during Boundary Scan Testing
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper proposes a Normalized Cross Correlation (NCC) based solution for integrating automated visual inspection with Boundary Scan Test (BST, IEEE Std. 1149.1). The proposed approach can serve as a guide when implementing an industrial BST station and it emerged as a necessity in the context of proliferation of such tests. BST procedures may include activation/deactivation of signaling LEDs mounted on the printed circuit boards (PCBs). Successful testing of such elements often relies on human visual inspection and manual confirmation, for example by key/button pressing. The aim of our work is to provide a low-cost alternative. By using XJTAG tools, NI LabVIEW, and MATLAB, we demonstrate the practical implications of visual inspection by means of NCC in an automated test scenario. Finally, a report on different integration strategies applied with the purpose of maximizing Device Under Test (DUT) coverage and reducing test design effort and costs, is discussed.
